svg.title: The variance bound is sufficient for unrestricted real observations when the count is at least two
svg.desc: Let T be the total and Q the sum of squares. Nonnegative squared deviations imply Q minus T squared over n is nonnegative. The graph for count three has boundary Q equals T squared over three. The region on and above the parabola admits unrestricted real observations; the region below does not. At total six, Q fourteen has example records one, two and three. At Q twelve, equality forces three repeated twos. At Q ten, Q minus twelve is negative, so no real records exist. For any count n at least two satisfying the bound, write mu equals T over n and d equals the square root of half the difference between Q and T squared over n. A witness consists of mu minus d, mu plus d and n minus two remaining copies of mu. With count one, the only observation is T and Q must equal T squared exactly. Integer or nonnegative restrictions require separate checks; unrestricted real feasibility does not establish them.
